summary.headline: Welspun Corp posted record quarterly EBITDA of INR756 crore (+35% YoY) and an INR25,750 crore order book, heavily US-weighted.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as robust, with the highest-ever quarterly EBITDA of INR756 crore, up 35% YoY, and ROCE above 20% annualised. Net cash rose to INR2,336 crore and the order book was about INR25,750 crore (~$2.7 billion), described as the strongest in company history and heavily loaded toward the US. Domestic DI pipe demand under Jal Jeevan Mission was weak on fund constraints and industry overcapacity, so the company shifted focus to exports and pig iron. Sintex remains under pressure from muted domestic demand, and management continues to invest in its dealer, distribution and branding base. Full-year guidance was not revised, which management attributed to a policy of giving realistic guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Strongest in company history; mid-call an analyst cited INR24,750 crore and management later said close to INR26,000 crore

financial_highlights.value: Guidance about $300 per tonne; current quarter slightly above

segments.name: US line pipe (Little Rock, HFIW/ERW and LSAW)
segments.commentary: Booked well through FY28 with FY29 discussions under way. The ERW/HFIW mill is commissioned and stabilised with orders being started. The LSAW plant is due by year-end. Order book split is about 75% export-to-Gulf Coast LNG and about 25% data centres.

segments.name: Saudi Arabia line pipe (KSA)
segments.commentary: Two facilities are progressing, with the first expected by Q2 and both progressively by Q3 FY27 per management. Competitive intensity is rising, and anti-dumping action on DI pipe imports is moving in the right direction.

segments.name: India DI pipes and pig iron
segments.commentary: Domestic Jal Jeevan Mission demand is under severe pressure. Capacity was scaled down and pig iron exports were ramped, with management calling the company one of the largest pig iron exporters this quarter. India LSAW exports run at about 150,000-200,000 tonnes a year.

segments.name: Sintex (B2C building products)
segments.commentary: Impacted by muted domestic demand. Management is expanding its dealer, distributor and influencer network quarter on quarter and continuing announced capex. No segment financials were given on the call.

segments.name: Welspun Specialty Steel (WSSL)
segments.commentary: Management said the project is on track and progressing as planned. No figures were given.

segments.name: EPIC (Saudi associate)
segments.commentary: Partial stake sale of about 3-4.5%. Welspun retains more than 22% and remains the largest shareholder, with no further dilution planned.

guidance_outlook: Full-year guidance was not raised. Management said it prefers realistic guidance and has met or exceeded guidance over the last four years.
Management stands by absolute EBITDA guidance and declined to guide on margins.
KSA and Little Rock capex projects are expected to be up and running by end-CY2026 and to contribute fully in FY28.
Management said no incremental capex beyond announced KSA and US projects; about 60-65% of that capex is complete with the balance in FY27.
Guardrails: ROCE above 20%, net debt to EBITDA below 1x, investment only in core geographies and products.
capex_capacity: Saudi and Little Rock capex is about 60-65% complete, with the cycle started about a year ago. Commissioning is expected by year-end and balance capex in FY27.
US ERW/HFIW mill has been commissioned and stabilised. LSAW plant is expected by end-FY27 (year-end).
KSA: two facilities expected to ramp progressively, with the first by Q2 and both by Q3 per management.
No new capacity planned in the US. Management said a new US plant needs about 18-24 months and new entrants would struggle.
Excess cash deployment (dividend, buyback, investment) is still under discussion; no decision yet.
demand_pricing: US demand described as very buoyant, with FY28 booked and FY29 discussions with midstream customers ongoing but not yet firm. Steel supply for FY29 is still being triangulated.
Data centres are about 25% of the current US mix versus LNG export at about 75%, and this is shifting toward data centres in new bookings.
Saudi: competition is rising, with other Indian players adding capacity. Management said the market is large enough for all and the company has more than 15 years on the ground.
Section 232 tariffs described as statute-based and durable, supporting US steel pricing.
The Saudi East-West pipeline expansion is in engagement stage, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is competitive intensity rising in Saudi line pipe and DI pipe, and what is the Saudi anti-dumping status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition is rising but the market is large enough for everyone, and the company has more than 15 years on the ground. Anti-dumping is progressing in the right direction, and the Saudi law requires imports to stop once domestic capacity is available.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected peak net debt for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No figures given. Management reiterated guardrails of ROCE above 20% and net debt to EBITDA below 1x, and said the balance sheet will get healthier with free cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA margin in Q1 sustainable and what is US EBITDA per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin is driven by raw material and product mix, so it will not guide on margin and stands by absolute EBITDA guidance. US EBITDA per tonne guidance is about $300, and current quarter is slightly above that.

qa_highlights.question: Why is full-year guidance not being raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers realistic guidance given project-based business and geopolitical uncertainty, and has met or exceeded guidance over the last four years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for the 26% GGBS (slag) associate stake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a mandatory and notional equity stake in a third-party company that is investing capex on the company's premises to convert slag into a saleable product, with no capex by Welspun.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any incremental capex or inorganic plan beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No incremental capex beyond announced projects. Management said there is nothing on the table for inorganic moves and the board will guide cash deployment.

risks_watch: Indian DI pipe demand under Jal Jeevan Mission is weak and management expects the pain to persist for a longer period. Watch pig iron export volume and margins.
FY29 US visibility depends on steel substrate pricing and supply, which management says is still being triangulated.
Rising Saudi competition from other Indian and local capacity additions.
Geopolitical disruption: some minor hiccups in KSA project timelines, though no capital equipment was affected.
Sintex remains loss-making on margin and its B2C investment load, with no profitability timeline given.
Management declined to provide US/India order book split and US volume breakup on the call; follow-up was offline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on US and KSA demand and execution, but cautious on India domestic and Sintex. Management was evasive on quarterly margins, volume split, FY29 specifics and guidance upgrades, pointing to year-on-year tracking.
key_quotes: We have delivered the highest ever quarterly EBITDA of INR756 crores, a 35% growth on a Y-on-Y basis.
We stand by to the absolute EBITDA numbers for which we give the guidance, number 1.
Right now, we have booked well through FY28, and we are already seeing clarity emerging on FY29 as well.
I think so this company need not to be looked on a quarter-on-quarter basis. I think so this is a company to be looked on a year-on-year basis.

growth.why: Full-year guidance was held, not raised; absolute EBITDA guidance stands and US EBITDA/tonne is guided near $300, backed by US line pipe bookings through FY28 (~INR25,750 crore order book) and KSA and Little Rock capacity (60-65% complete) due to come live by end-CY2026, though the India DI business faces severe demand pressure.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA of INR756 crore (+35% YoY) and US EBITDA/tonne slightly above the ~$300 guide, but management declined to guide on margins and cites raw material and mix swings.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: KSA line pipe facilities (first by Q2, both by Q3 FY27) and Little Rock LSAW (by year-end) are 60-65% complete and firmly committed; the ERW/HFIW mill is already commissioned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: US line pipe is booked through FY28 and new Little Rock and KSA capacity comes live by year-end, though India DI volumes are under severe Jal Jeevan Mission pressure.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said no incremental capex beyond the announced KSA and US projects and is not committing to other capex; no new US plant is planned, and excess cash deployment is still undecided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Full-year guidance was held, not raised; management prefers realistic guidance despite the strong Q1 and only stands by absolute EBITDA numbers.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: India DI demand is under severe pressure and KSA timelines have already slipped (first facility Q2 to Q3), with geopolitical hiccups and rising Saudi competition as watch items.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product launches were discussed beyond the commissioning of existing US and KSA capacity.

rows.label: Record INR25,750 crore order book, US FY28 booked
rows.why: Order book is about INR25,750 crore (~$2.7 billion), strongest in company history, with US line pipe booked through FY28 and about 75% LNG export and 25% data centres.

rows.label: Net cash INR2,336 crore, net debt/EBITDA below 1x guardrail
rows.why: Net cash rose to INR2,336 crore and management reiterated net debt to EBITDA below 1x with free cash flow expected to strengthen the balance sheet.

rows.label: Saudi anti-dumping on DI pipe imports
rows.why: Management said anti-dumping is moving in the right direction and Saudi law requires imports to stop once domestic capacity is available, but no timeline or figures were given.

tone.note: Management was confident on US demand, FY28 bookings and KSA/Little Rock execution, but cautious on India DI and Sintex and evasive on margins, volume split and FY29 specifics; analysts pushed on Saudi competition, sustainability of margin and why guidance was not raised.

quality.why: Quarterly EBITDA rose 35% YoY to a record INR756 crore, but the brief does not state whether volume, price or mix drove it, gives no volume growth figure, and lists no one-off items; management attributes margin to raw material and product mix without quantifying either.
